# check_computer_archives

[← Command index](README.md)

Find Windows executables that are larger than 4092 MB.

## Synopsis

```
check_computer_archives [options]
```

## Description

Finds every `.exe` file under the input path (or takes the one file given) and checks
its size. The run stops with an error at the first one larger than 4092 MB
(4,290,772,992 bytes), naming the file. 4092 MB is the volume size backup_tool uses
when it splits archives.

Nothing is written or changed, and there is no confirmation prompt.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | An `.exe` file, or a directory searched recursively for them; must exist. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Check the installers in a folder of computer games

```bash
check_computer_archives -i /path/to/computer/games
```
